# Fanfarr v0.3.0

Fanfarr finds theme music for a Plex library, writes it beside the media as a
local `theme.mp3`, and keeps a permanent record of what it did and why. What
follows has accumulated since v0.2.0.

## Long themes are cropped as they arrive

A theme is often two minutes of slow build-up, and Plex plays it from the top.
v0.2.0 could crop one when you asked. Now the ones worth cropping are cropped on
the way in: a theme longer than the threshold in Settings -- three minutes by
default -- is written at the crop length instead, ninety seconds by default. It
happens in the same pass as the download and before the loudness pass, so a
cropped theme stays level-matched with the rest of the library, and it costs one
encode rather than two.

The threshold is the unattended rule, and this is the only path that applies it.
A trim you ask for -- **Suggest a crop** on an item page, or **Trim** in the
library -- takes the crop length as its own floor, so a theme of any length is
cut to the length you asked for, and only one too short to hold the crop is
declined.

## Trim a whole selection

Ticking rows in the library and choosing **Trim current themes** queues a crop
for each of them, one at a time. It cuts the file that is already there rather
than downloading it again, so a library-wide tidy-up needs no network, and the
work is cancellable from Activity like any other bulk action.

## The crop can be switched off

Theme crop in Settings now has a switch. Off, nothing is fetched or decoded on
its own and no crop is suggested. Trimming by hand still works: that switch is
about what Fanfarr does unattended, not about the editor.

## Redownload a theme from its source

Cropping re-encodes, and trimming the same title a few times accumulates
generations. **Redownload** on an item page fetches the original again, starts
over from one, and keeps the crop you had chosen. The source cache is refreshed
in the same step, so the cached copy is not a generation behind the theme.

## Fixed

- Applying a theme whose source was already in the cache crashed, every time.
  The cache is what makes trimming and then re-applying fast, so this was the
  common path rather than an edge case.
- A viewership graph was being read as a length. A 275-second theme with a
  hundred-second graph was declined as too short without asking the audio, which
  is the fallback that exists for exactly that case.
- A theme shorter than the crop was reported as "no window could be found",
  which was not true of it. It now says that it is shorter than the crop.
- The application log records the range that was written, including a crop
  nothing had asked for, so a theme that arrives short can be explained later.
- Tests no longer run database cases concurrently. SQLite takes one writer at a
  time, and two concurrent cases were failing whichever tests happened to run
  beside them -- often in a setup, before the test body had started.

## Upgrading

Pull the new image and restart; the database migrates itself on boot. Three
things worth knowing:

- Cropping on download applies from the moment you upgrade. If you would rather
  themes arrived at full length, turn the switch off in Theme crop.
- Themes already written are left alone. To apply the new lengths to what you
  have, tick the rows you want in the library and choose **Trim current themes**.
- A theme shorter than the threshold is still written whole: nothing is clamped
  or padded to fit.
